types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being, typically identified by name and role. Also called Individual, Person, Human, Individual. Examples: Luigi Mangione, Brian Thompson, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, James McDonald.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Person' aligns with schema.org's Person class, which represents individual human beings. Mentions like 'Luigi Mangione' and 'Brian Thompson' are valid instances.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a shared purpose or goal. Also called Company, Institution, Corporation, Entity. Examples: UnitedHealthcare, Manhattan D.A.’s Office, the insurance giant, the healthcare insurer.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Organization' matches schema.org's Organization class, which represents groups of people with shared goals. Mentions like 'UnitedHealthcare' fit this category.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Date' matches schema.org's Date data type, which represents calendar dates. Mentions like '2024-12-04' are valid instances.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Weapon: An object used to inflict harm or kill. Also called Arm, Instrument, Tool, Device. Examples: 3-D printed pistol, the gun used, the 3-D printed gun.

chosen_type.label: Weapon
chosen_type.definition: An object designed or used to inflict harm or kill.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a weapon. The mention '3-D printed pistol' is a weapon, so a new type is needed.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

types.embedding_query_text: System Examples: UnitedHealthcare’s healthcare system, the healthcare industry, health insurance system.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'System' refers to a healthcare system, aligning with schema.org's MedicalOrganization, which represents medical institutions like 'UnitedHealthcare’s healthcare system'.

candidates.label: HealthInsurancePlan
candidates.comment: A HealthInsurancePlan is an intangible financial product that specifies coverage and costs for medical services, such as PPOs, EPOs, and HMOs. Also called medical insurance policy, healthcare plan, health coverage. Examples: Blue Cross PPO, Kaiser Permanente HMO, Medicare Advantage plan. Distinct from HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification, which describes patient costs under a plan, and HealthPlanFormulary, which details drug coverage.

candidates.label: HealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanNetwork is an intangible collection of healthcare providers, such as doctors and hospitals, that contract with a health insurance plan to provide services at negotiated rates. Also called provider network, insurance network, healthcare provider group. Examples: an HMO network, a PPO network, a specific hospital system affiliated with an insurer.

candidates.label: HealthPlanFormulary
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanFormulary is an intangible specification for the costs and coverage of prescription drugs under a given health insurance plan. Also called drug list, prescription drug coverage, medication formulary. Examples: a list of covered medications, a tiered drug pricing schedule, a preferred drug list. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification, which covers general patient costs beyond just drugs.

candidates.label: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification is an intangible description of the patient's financial responsibilities, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance, under a specific health insurance plan. Also called patient cost details, insurance out-of-pocket, healthcare expense breakdown. Examples: a document detailing a plan's deductible, copay for specialist visits, coinsurance percentage. Distinct from HealthInsurancePlan, which is the overall policy, and HealthPlanFormulary, which focuses specifically on prescription drug costs.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A physical or geographic place where an event occurs. Also called Place, Site, Venue, Area. Examples: New York City, Pennsylvania McDonald’s, Manhattan, the city.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Location' matches schema.org's Place class, which represents physical sites. Mentions like 'New York City' and 'Pennsylvania McDonald’s' are valid instances.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: TimeSpan Examples: 2024-12-04 to 2024-12-04, the day of the killing.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'TimeSpan' is a specific calendar date range, which matches schema.org's Date data type. Mentions like '2024-12-04 to 2024-12-04' are valid instances.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryAmount Examples: 50 billion, $50 billion, over $50 billion.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'MonetaryAmount' aligns with schema.org's MonetaryAmount class, which represents financial values. The mention '50 billion' fits this type.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: PaymentMethodType
candidates.comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.

types.embedding_query_text: SentenceRange Examples: 24 to 30 years, 24-30 years, federal guidelines sentence.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'SentenceRange' refers to a time span, matching schema.org's Duration class. The mention '24 to 30 years' represents a period of time.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: MaximumDoseSchedule
candidates.comment: A medical dose schedule specifying the highest recommended safe dosage for a drug or supplement, as advised by an authority or manufacturer. Also called max dosage, upper dose limit, safe dose ceiling. Examples: "maximum 2 tablets per day", "not to exceed 100mg daily", "maximum single dose 500mg".

candidates.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
candidates.comment: A PostalCodeRangeSpecification is a StructuredValue indicating a range of postal codes, defined by a beginning and ending code. Also called zip code range, postcode boundary. Examples: 90210-90215, 00000-99999, a range of postal codes for a delivery zone.

types.embedding_query_text: Sentence: A legal punishment imposed by a court. Also called Penalty, Punishment, Judgment, Sentence. Examples: life imprisonment, maximum penalty, life in prison.

chosen_type.label: Sentence
chosen_type.definition: A legal punishment imposed by a court.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a legal sentence. The mention 'life imprisonment' is a valid instance, so a new type is needed.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A specific occurrence or action in time. Also called Occurrence, Action, Happening, Incident. Examples: Mangione's arrest at Pennsylvania McDonald’s on Dec. 9, 2024, arrest event, Dec. 9 arrest.
mentions: Mangione's arrest at Pennsylvania McDonald’s on Dec. 9, 2024

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.
